uncited: Gradient estimation methods approximate the volume gradient at sample locations to provide surface normals for shading iso-surfaces, solving the problem of how to derive accurate normals from discrete scalar field data.

The family shares the goal of estimating the gradient $
abla f$ of a scalar field $f$ to approximate the surface normal $\mathbf{n} =  rac{
abla f}{\|
abla f\|}$.
Calculate the gradient at specific sample locations.
A critical shared pitfall is that the estimated gradient depends heavily on the sample location and distance.
The central difference method calculates the gradient using samples symmetrically around the point of interest.
This method computes the derivative of the cubic-spline interpolation function.
Originated in the context of iso-surface volume rendering for medical applications, these methods were evaluated for speed and accuracy.
